title: Gather scattered @Value into @ConfigurationProperties
summary: Two classes disagreed on the default mail.port, and the record that fixed it stopped a missing host from failing startup.

turns.user: mail.* @Value is all over the place. MailService defaults port to 587 and DigestJob defaults it to 25 lol. want one place

assistant.body: Here's the plan: one record bound with @ConfigurationProperties becomes the single source of truth for mail.*, so two defaults cannot drift apart again. In Boot 3 a record with a single constructor binds through it without @ConstructorBinding. @ConfigurationPropertiesScan on the application class registers it.

turns.user: did DigestJob too. but staging was missing mail.host and it booted fine, then blew up on first send. it used to refuse to start??

assistant.body: Good catch, I missed that. @Value fails at startup when a placeholder cannot be resolved, but binding to a record just leaves a missing key as null. With @Validated and @NotBlank the record is checked at startup and a missing value stops the boot. Note: this needs spring-boot-starter-validation on the classpath.
